region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Paddy Overview & Strategic Recommendations (Punjab/Ludhiana)
rule: For central Punjab, use recommended PAU varieties like PR 126 (short duration), PR 121, PR 128, or PR 130. Manage water with 15 days standing water followed strictly by Alternate Wetting & Drying (AWD). Complete urea in 3 splits (by 35 days for PR 126, by 42 days for others). Do NOT apply DAP if DAP was applied to the preceding wheat crop.
conditions: Applicable across typical medium fertility canal/tubewell irrigated soils in Punjab.
actionable_guidance: Follow the PAU package of practices: Avoid continuous flooding beyond day 15 to conserve groundwater and reduce greenhouse gases. Stop irrigation 15 days prior to harvest.
reasoning: Saves 20-25% water, lowers electricity/diesel cost, prevents root rot, and reduces pest pressure.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Kharif Crops (Kharif/Paddy)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Paddy Early Stage Irrigation: 0-15 Days Continuous Standing Water
rule: Maintain continuous shallow standing water (4-5 cm) in the field for the first 15 days after transplanting.
conditions: First 15 days after transplanting seedlings into puddled field.
actionable_guidance: Do not allow the field to dry out during these initial 15 days. Keep standing water depth around 4 to 5 cm.
reasoning: Standing water during the first 15 days is essential for healthy root establishment and suppresses weed seeds from germinating in the puddled soil.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Kharif Crops (Kharif/Paddy)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
growth_stage: 16 days after transplanting to flowering (vegetative & reproductive phase)
title: Paddy AWD Protocol: Alternate Wetting & Drying (16 Days to Flowering)
rule: Do NOT keep continuous standing water after day 15. Apply irrigation 2 days after standing water has completely infiltrated/seeped into the soil.
conditions: From Day 16 until flowering. Do not let soil develop deep cracks.
actionable_guidance: Check the field daily: when standing ponded water disappears, wait for 2 days. On the 2nd day after drying, apply the next irrigation (5-7 cm).
reasoning: Intermittent drying promotes deep root proliferation, aerates the root zone, cuts water usage by ~25%, and curtails sheath blight and brown planthopper outbreaks.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Kharif Crops (Kharif/Paddy)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
growth_stage: Flowering, Panicle Emergence & Grain Filling (milking stage)
title: Paddy Flowering & Grain Filling Critical Irrigation
rule: Ensure adequate soil moisture is continuously available during flowering, panicle emergence, and milking. Apply irrigation without delay as soon as surface water disappears.
conditions: Active flowering, heading, and milky grain development stages.
actionable_guidance: Do not subject crop to dry spells during panicle emergence and grain filling. Irrigate promptly when soil surface begins to dry.
reasoning: Moisture deficit during flowering and milking causes pollen sterility and incomplete grain filling, resulting in empty glumes / high chaffiness (thotha / ਥੋਥਾ).
source: PAU Package of Practices for Kharif Crops (Kharif/Paddy)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Paddy Pre-Harvest Irrigation Cutoff
rule: Stop all irrigation completely 15 days before the intended date of harvesting.
conditions: Crop entering physiological maturity (golden yellowing of grains and straw).
actionable_guidance: Drain remaining water and withhold further irrigation 15 days before combine harvesting.
reasoning: Ensures uniform grain ripening, reduces grain moisture content for procurement, and firms the soil to allow combine harvesters without bogging down.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Kharif Crops (Kharif/Paddy)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Paddy Recommended Fertilizer Doses & Standard 3-Split Urea Schedule
rule: Total fertilizer per acre for medium fertility: 90 kg Urea (40-42 kg N), applied in 3 equal splits: (1) Basal at transplanting (30 kg), (2) 21 days after transplanting (30 kg), (3) 42 days after transplanting (30 kg).
conditions: Standard duration varieties (PR 121, 128, 130, etc.). Omit basal dose if green manure (dhaincha/sunhemp) was incorporated.
actionable_guidance: Apply 30 kg Urea per acre at transplanting, 30 kg at 3 weeks (21 days), and 30 kg at 6 weeks (42 days). Apply into moist soil, not deep standing flood water.
reasoning: Splitting nitrogen matches crop uptake curves, reduces leaching and volatilization losses, and avoids excessive lush growth.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Kharif Crops (Kharif/Paddy)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Paddy PR 126 Short-Duration Variety Urea Fast-Track Schedule
rule: For short-duration variety PR 126, all 90 kg Urea (or 3 splits of 30 kg) must be completely applied within 35 days after transplanting.
conditions: PR 126 variety planted.
actionable_guidance: Apply split 1 at transplanting (30 kg), split 2 around 18-20 days (30 kg), and final split 3 by 35 days (30 kg). Do not apply urea after 35 days for PR 126.
reasoning: PR 126 has a compact vegetative cycle (~93 days after transplanting). Late urea delays maturity, invites sheath blight and leaf folder, and leads to lodging.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Kharif Crops (Kharif/Paddy)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Paddy Phosphorus (DAP) Carryover Rule from Wheat
rule: If the recommended dose of DAP (55 kg/acre) was applied to the preceding wheat crop, do NOT apply DAP to the paddy crop.
conditions: Paddy grown in rotation following wheat that received recommended phosphorus.
actionable_guidance: Do not purchase or apply DAP for paddy if wheat was adequately fertilized. Save your money.
reasoning: Submerged anaerobic conditions in puddled paddy soils release fixed phosphorus from the soil matrix and wheat residue, meeting the entire phosphorus need of rice without extra fertilizer.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Kharif Crops (Kharif/Paddy)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: PAU Golden Rule: Strict Cutoff for Late Urea Application in Paddy
rule: Never apply urea after 42 days (after panicle initiation) for standard varieties or after 35 days for PR 126.
conditions: Crop older than 42 days (or PR 126 older than 35 days).
actionable_guidance: If crop appears pale after the cutoff date, do not broadcast urea. Check for root health or micro-nutrient deficiency instead.
reasoning: Late nitrogen prolongs vegetative stage, prevents synchronous flowering, causes lodging (falling), weakens cell walls, and attracts severe Stem Borer and Brown Planthopper attacks.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Kharif Crops (Kharif/Paddy)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Paddy Leaf Folder (ਪੱਤਾ ਲਪੇਟ / Patta Lapet) Symptoms & ETL Trigger
rule: Spray insecticide ONLY when the Economic Threshold Level (ETL) exceeds 10% damaged/folded leaves.
conditions: White papery longitudinal streaks with leaves folded lengthwise.
actionable_guidance: Inspect 20 random hills across the field. Count folded leaves. If damaged leaves are below 10%, do not spray chemical insecticide; predatory spiders and beneficial insects will naturally control them.
reasoning: Paddy plants compensate naturally for minor foliage loss; unnecessary early sprays wipe out natural biocontrol predators and lead to secondary pest resurgence (BPH).
source: PAU Package of Practices for Kharif Crops (Kharif/Paddy)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Paddy Stem Borer (ਤਣਾ ਛੇਦਕ / Tana Chhedak) Symptoms & ETL Trigger
rule: Chemical control is warranted only if ETL of >5% 'dead hearts' at vegetative stage or >2% 'white ears' (whiteheads) at panicle stage is reached.
conditions: Dead hearts (central shoot dries up and pulls out easily) or white empty erect panicles.
actionable_guidance: Monitor field weekly. If threshold is breached, spray PAU recommended insecticide (such as Cartap hydrochloride 50 SP @ 1 kg/acre or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC @ 60 ml/acre in 100 L water).
reasoning: Targeted chemical spray prevents yield-limiting stem damage without overuse of broad-spectrum toxic chemicals.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Kharif Crops (Kharif/Paddy)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Zinc Deficiency (Khaira Disease / ਖਹਿਰਾ ਰੋਗ) Symptoms & Corrective Action
rule: Zinc deficiency causes lower leaves to develop brown/rusty patches, small leaf size, and stunted growth. Correct with foliar spray of 0.5% Zinc Sulphate (21%) + 0.5% unslaked lime or soil application.
conditions: Appears 2-3 weeks after transplanting, common in alkaline/intensively cropped soils.
actionable_guidance: For acute symptoms: Dissolve 1 kg Zinc Sulphate (21%) and 0.5 kg unslaked lime in 200 liters of water per acre, spray immediately. Repeat after 7-10 days if symptoms persist. In soil: apply 10 kg Zinc Sulphate (21%) or 6.5 kg Zinc Sulphate (33%) per acre at puddling.
reasoning: Unslaked lime neutralizes the acidity of zinc sulphate, preventing foliar leaf burn while rapidly restoring photosynthetic zinc enzymes.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Kharif Crops (Kharif/Paddy)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Iron Deficiency (Yellowing of Young Leaves in Light Soils)
rule: Youngest upper leaves turn pale yellow or ivory white between veins, especially in permeable sandy soils under tubewell water.
conditions: Light-textured/sandy soils, excessive water percolation.
actionable_guidance: Spray 1.0% Ferrous Sulphate solution (1 kg Ferrous Sulphate / hara kasis dissolved in 100 liters of water per acre) 2 to 3 times at weekly intervals. Keep field continuously submerged for a few days.
reasoning: Submergence converts unavailable ferric iron into plant-available ferrous iron ($Fe^{2+}$). Foliar iron rapidly relieves chlorophyll synthesis blockage.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Kharif Crops (Kharif/Paddy)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Weather Decision Gate: Irrigation & Urea Application vs Rainfall Forecast
rule: If rain > 5 mm is forecasted within the next 48 hours, withhold irrigation. If rain or wind > 15 km/h is forecasted in the next 24 hours, postpone urea top-dressing and chemical sprays.
conditions: Monsoon showers forecasted or impending rain events.
actionable_guidance: Check weather forecast: delay irrigation if rain is arriving. Never broadcast urea right before a downpour to avoid runoff and leaching losses.
reasoning: Saves pumping energy/diesel costs and prevents nitrate runoff into drainage ditches.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Kharif Crops & Agro-meteorology Advisories

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Wheat Overview & Strategic Recommendations (Punjab/Ludhiana)
rule: Wheat requires 4-5 stage-dependent irrigations. Crown Root Initiation (CRI at 20-25 DAS) is the single most critical stage. Apply full DAP (55 kg/acre) + 1/2 Urea at sowing, and finish remaining Urea at first irrigation (CRI). Complete all nitrogen before 2nd irrigation. Guard against Yellow Rust and high wind lodging in Feb/March.
conditions: Rabi season cultivation following paddy or cotton in Punjab.
actionable_guidance: Use certified seed, timely sowing (Nov 1-15 for long varieties), drill fertilizer below seed, and prioritize irrigation according to physiological stage rather than fixed days.
reasoning: Crown root establishment and spike development set the yield foundation; balanced timely nutrition avoids diseases and late season lodging.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Rabi Crops (Rabi/Wheat)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
growth_stage: Crown Root Initiation / CRI (20-25 days after sowing)
title: Wheat 1st Irrigation: Crown Root Initiation (CRI Stage) — Mandatory
rule: Apply the 1st irrigation strictly at 20 to 25 days after sowing (CRI stage). This is the single most critical irrigation of the wheat crop.
conditions: 20-25 days after sowing (DAS). Even if seasonal water is constrained, this irrigation must not be missed.
actionable_guidance: Irrigate field lightly at 20-25 DAS. Broadcast the second half of Urea (45-55 kg/acre) immediately before or right after this irrigation.
reasoning: Crown roots (the permanent root system that anchors the plant and feeds tillers) develop at this node. Missing or delaying this irrigation causes permanent root stunting and drastically cuts ear-bearing tillers.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Rabi Crops (Rabi/Wheat)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Wheat Intermediate Irrigations: Tillering (40-45 DAS) & Jointing/Booting (70-75 DAS)
rule: Apply 2nd irrigation at Tillering stage (40-45 DAS) and 3rd irrigation at Late Jointing / Booting stage (70-75 DAS), adjusting for winter rains (Western Disturbances).
conditions: 40-75 DAS vegetative to reproductive transition.
actionable_guidance: Check rainfall received: if substantial winter rain occurred, delay irrigation. Ensure soil has good moisture as spikelets and earheads form inside the boot leaf.
reasoning: Moisture deficit at jointing and booting reduces spike length, number of spikelets per spike, and overall biomass.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Rabi Crops (Rabi/Wheat)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
growth_stage: Flowering (90-95 DAS) & Grain Filling / Milking (105-115 DAS)
title: Wheat Flowering & Grain Filling Irrigation (Wind Speed Guardrail)
rule: Provide irrigation at flowering (90-95 DAS) and soft dough (105-115 DAS). CRITICAL: Never irrigate when wind speed is high (>12-15 km/h).
conditions: Feb to March period during anthesis and grain filling.
actionable_guidance: Check weather forecast and calm wind hours (often early morning or late evening). Avoid irrigating on windy afternoons.
reasoning: Wet soft soil combined with tall, top-heavy grain-laden wheat heads easily results in lodging (crop falling over). Lodged wheat suffers 30-50% yield loss and shriveled grains.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Rabi Crops (Rabi/Wheat)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Wheat Pre-Harvest Irrigation Cut-off Rule
rule: Stop all irrigation completely by the end of March (as grain enters hard dough stage).
conditions: Grain turning hard and foliage turning golden yellow.
actionable_guidance: Do not apply irrigation in April prior to harvest.
reasoning: Allows natural ripening and uniform drying of grains, preventing mold development and harvest delays.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Rabi Crops (Rabi/Wheat)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Wheat Recommended Doses & Application Timeline
rule: Recommended per acre for medium fertility: 110 kg Urea (50 kg N), 55 kg DAP (25 kg P2O5), and 20 kg MOP (if potassium deficient). Apply full DAP + 1/2 Urea (55 kg) at sowing drilled below seed; apply remaining 1/2 Urea (55 kg) at 1st irrigation (20-25 DAS).
conditions: Standard wheat cultivation. (If preceding crop was green-manured, reduce total urea to 90 kg).
actionable_guidance: Drill all DAP and half Urea at sowing with a seed-cum-fertilizer drill. Top-dress the remaining half Urea right before or after the 1st irrigation at 20-25 days.
reasoning: Phosphorus is immobile and needed right at germination for root growth. Nitrogen split ensures adequate nutrition during peak tillering without early leaching.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Rabi Crops (Rabi/Wheat)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: PAU Golden Rule: Strict Nitrogen Cutoff for Wheat Before 2nd Irrigation
rule: Complete all Nitrogen/Urea application BEFORE the 2nd irrigation (maximum by 45-50 DAS). Never apply urea late during jointing or booting stages.
conditions: Crop beyond 45-50 days after sowing.
actionable_guidance: Do not broadcast urea after 45-50 DAS. If wheat appears light green late in the season, check for Yellow Rust or spray 2-3% Urea foliar spray rather than broadcasting granular urea.
reasoning: Late urea broadcast creates succulent leaves that make wheat highly prone to Yellow Rust, powdery mildew, and late season lodging in March winds.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Rabi Crops (Rabi/Wheat)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
growth_stage: 30 to 35 days after sowing (2-3 days after 1st irrigation)
title: Gullidanda (Phalaris minor / ਗੁੱਲੀ ਡੰਡਾ) Herbicide Timing & Protocol
rule: Spray PAU recommended weedicides for Gullidanda (Canary grass) strictly within 30-35 DAS, 2-3 days after the 1st irrigation when optimum soil moisture (wattar) is present.
conditions: 30-35 DAS, weeds at 2-3 leaf stage.
actionable_guidance: Use a flat-fan nozzle and 150 liters of water per acre. Spray recommended chemicals (e.g., Clodinafop 15 WP @ 160 g/acre or Pinoxaden 5.1 EC @ 400 ml/acre or Metribuzin combinations as recommended by PAU). Do not spray in dry soil.
reasoning: Gullidanda beyond 3-4 leaf stage develops resistance and is difficult to kill. Post-irrigation moisture is necessary for systemic herbicide translocation.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Rabi Crops (Rabi/Wheat)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Yellow Rust (Puccinia striiformis / ਪੀਲੀ ਕੁੰਗੀ / Peeli Kungi) Diagnosis & Emergency Treatment
rule: Yellow Rust appears as bright yellow powdery stripes/pustules along the leaf veins that rub off on fingers like yellow turmeric powder. Upon first appearance, spray immediately with Propiconazole 25 EC (Tilt) @ 200 ml in 200 L water per acre or Nativo 75 WG @ 120 g/acre.
conditions: Cool (10-20°C), humid, cloudy weather in January and February.
actionable_guidance: Scout fields weekly in Jan/Feb. If yellow pustules appear, spray Tilt 25 EC (Propiconazole) or Nativo immediately. Direct the spray thoroughly over the foliage. Avoid delaying even 2-3 days as rust spreads rapidly on wind currents.
reasoning: Yellow Rust destroys photosynthetic leaf area and can cause up to 70% yield collapse in susceptible varieties if left untreated during grain development.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Rabi Crops (Rabi/Wheat)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
growth_stage: Vegetative stage following heavy irrigation or rain
title: Wheat Yellowing Diagnosis: Waterlogging vs Yellow Rust vs Deficiency
rule: Differentiate leaf yellowing: (1) Generalized pale yellow lower leaves after heavy water/rain = Temporary nitrogen leaching/suffocation from waterlogging; (2) Yellow powdery stripes = Yellow Rust; (3) Interveinal greyish-pink/white necrotic spots in sandy soils = Manganese deficiency.
conditions: Yellowing noticed in January or February.
actionable_guidance: If caused by waterlogging: drain standing water immediately and spray 3% Urea solution (3 kg urea dissolved in 100 L water per acre). If Yellow Rust: spray Propiconazole (Tilt 25 EC). If Manganese deficiency: spray 0.5% Manganese Sulphate.
reasoning: Accurate differential diagnosis prevents farmers from mistakenly buying expensive fungicides for waterlogging or throwing harmful extra soil urea during rust infection.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Rabi Crops (Rabi/Wheat)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Wheat Aphid (ਚੇਪਾ / Chepa / Maho) Symptoms & Threshold
rule: Aphids suck sap from tender earheads and leaves during warmer March days. Spray ONLY if the population exceeds the Economic Threshold Level of 5 aphids per ear head.
conditions: March warming period during heading and milk stages.
actionable_guidance: Sample 20 ears across the field. If population is below 5 aphids per ear head, do not spray. If above ETL, spray Thiamethoxam 25 WG @ 20 g or Rogor (Dimethoate 30 EC) @ 150 ml in 100 L water per acre.
reasoning: Beneficial ladybird beetles and syrphid flies naturally consume aphids; spraying below ETL wastes money and destroys beneficial predators.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Rabi Crops (Rabi/Wheat)

region: Ludhiana & Central Plain Zone of Punjab
title: Wheat High Wind & Lodging Weather Gate
rule: Never apply irrigation when wind speeds exceed 12-15 km/h during February and March, especially at grain-filling stages.
conditions: Crop with heavy grain heads; surface wind forecasted.
actionable_guidance: Check wind forecast before opening tubewell/canal gate. Irrigate during calm morning/evening hours or postpone until wind subsides.
reasoning: Soil softens upon wetting; wind force against tall heavy earheads pulls roots out of the mud, knocking the crop flat (lodging), crippling combine harvest and causing severe yield loss.
source: PAU Package of Practices for Rabi Crops (Rabi/Wheat)
